comparison: Both evaluate CPK3 genetic screen data (C53-C56) positively. OpenEval finds the experimental design appropriate with supporting data in Figure 1A-B. Peer reviewers explicitly praised this work as 'masterful and very conclusive' with no concerns raised about the genetic findings.

Both address CPK3 knockout and overexpression phenotypes (C65-C70). OpenEval finds claims supported by Figure 1C-E data across independent lines. Peer reviewers confirmed the work 'clearly demonstrate' CPK3 specificity in viral spread, with Reviewer 1 finding the identification 'very convincing.'

Both evaluate kinase activity requirement (C76) and membrane localization (C81-C82). OpenEval finds strong support from complementation data. Peer reviewers raised concerns about imaging quality for PM localization claims, stating 'PM localisation and its non-PM localised form look similar' with insufficient imaging evidence, creating uncertainty despite genetic data.

Both address CPK3 membrane localization requirement (C81-C82). OpenEval finds genetic evidence from CPK3G2A complementation strong. Peer reviewers questioned imaging quality supporting PM localization, noting 'no PM stain or marker construct used' and insufficient confocal imaging quality.

Both evaluate in vitro kinase assay data (C57-C60) showing CPK3 phosphorylates REM1.2. OpenEval finds claims supported by Figure 1 supplement 2. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about these standard biochemical assays, implicitly supporting the specificity findings.

Both address CPK3 diffusion dynamics upon infection (C84-C86, C89). OpenEval finds spt-PALM data quantitatively demonstrates reduced diffusion and increased confinement. Peer Reviewer 1 acknowledged 'sptPALM data conclusions are nice and fit the narrative' but raised serious concerns about signal-to-noise ratio, particle separation, and conversion laser settings, creating uncertainty about measurement robustness.

Both evaluate CPK3CA constitutively active mutant dynamics (C94-C98). OpenEval finds support from spt-PALM showing more immobile molecules and confined motion. Peer reviewers noted CPK3CA 'strengthens the authors claims' but expressed concerns about underlying spt-PALM data quality affecting reliability of these measurements.

Both address PI4P effects on CPK3CA organization (C101-C105). OpenEval finds fenpropimorph and SAC1 data support that PI4P regulates but is not required for nanodomain formation. Peer reviewers raised concerns about confocal imaging quality being 'simply not sufficient' and noted better resolution methods (Airyscan) were available but not used.

Both evaluate CPK3 expression level data (C77-C78). OpenEval finds RT-qPCR and western blot support post-translational regulation. Peer reviewers did not question these straightforward control experiments, implicitly supporting the conclusion that the mechanism involves protein dynamics rather than expression changes.

Both address REM expression levels (C123-C124). OpenEval finds RT-qPCR and western blot data support post-translational regulation of REM function. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about these standard control experiments.

Perfect agreement on REM mutant phenotypes (C117-C122). OpenEval finds strong genetic evidence from additive effects and systemic propagation data. Peer Reviewer 2 found 'compelling evidence' through 'logical reverse genetics experiments,' and no specific concerns were raised about REM mutant phenotyping.

Both evaluate REM1.2 diffusion dynamics (C125-C129). OpenEval finds spt-PALM data support increased diffusion without nanodomain changes. Peer reviewers raised two concerns: general spt-PALM data quality issues, and specifically that 'remorins are involved in a lot of nano domain controlled processes' so authors haven't 'conclusively demonstrated' effects are solely due to CPK3 interaction, requesting negative controls with other PM proteins.

Both address genetic epistasis (C133-C134) and pathway interdependence (C145-C146). OpenEval finds lack of additive effect in quadruple mutant provides classic genetic evidence for same pathway function. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly confirmed authors 'clearly demonstrate' interdependence, and editor's summary noted 'solid evidence' for protein interactions in defense response.

Both evaluate overall CPK3-REM interdependence model (C145-C146). OpenEval finds reciprocal dependence represents major conceptual advance. Peer reviewers confirmed the work 'clearly demonstrate' interdependence with 'solid evidence,' though noted 'limited discussion' of mechanisms.

Both address CPK3-dependent regulation of REM1.2 dynamics (C136). OpenEval finds strong evidence from spt-PALM showing REM1.2 diffusion changes require CPK3. Peer reviewers acknowledged this 'goes part way' to support claims but noted general spt-PALM quality concerns and lack of simultaneous two-color imaging weakens the evidence.

Both evaluate reciprocal dependence showing CPK3 dynamics require REMs (C137-C138). OpenEval finds this demonstrates mutual dependence as a key finding. Peer reviewers noted the interdependence is 'clearly demonstrate[d]' but raised concerns about lack of two-color imaging and general spt-PALM data quality creating uncertainty.

Both address membrane localization requirement for CPK3 regulation of REM dynamics (C140-C142). OpenEval finds spt-PALM data support this requirement, paralleling earlier complementation findings. Peer reviewers raised concerns about spt-PALM data quality and noted these are transient N. benthamiana experiments rather than stable Arabidopsis lines.

Both evaluate colocalization data (C143-C144). OpenEval finds random colocalization reasonable given potential transient interactions, though speculative. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly criticized imaging as 'too noisy and no clear conclusions can be made' and stated 'kiss and go model...without two colour imaging of both proteins at the same time, the claims are much stronger than the evidence,' marking this UNSUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates CPK3 dynamics under infection and with CPK3CA (C106-C107) as UNCERTAIN, noting correlation between altered dynamics and activation is suggestive but lacks direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these interpretive claims about the relationship between dynamics and activation.

OpenEval finds literature citations establishing CPK3-REM biochemical relationships (C108-C112) well-supported. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background/context claims from prior literature.
OpenEval finds citations supporting REM functional redundancy (C113-C116) reasonable based on shared interactome. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these literature-based context claims.

OpenEval rates claim about REMs regulating CPK3 nanodomain formation (C139) as UNCERTAIN, noting data in supplement not fully presented and mechanistic basis unclear. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate this specific supplemental claim.

OpenEval evaluates high-level interpretive claims (C14-C15) about opposite dynamics contrasting with canonical models and the overall PM-based mechanism. These broad conceptual claims were not separately evaluated by peer reviewers, who focused on specific experimental evidence.
